q.t: The Earth turning about its own axis is called…
q.e: Rotation is spinning about an axis; revolution is going around another object.

q.t: About how long does the Earth take for one rotation?
q.e: One rotation takes about 24 hours — one day.

q.t: About how long does the Earth take to revolve around the Sun?
q.e: One revolution takes about 365¼ days — one year.

q.t: Day and night happen because of the Earth's…
q.e: As the Earth spins, places turn into and out of the sunlight.

q.t: The path of the Earth around the Sun is called its…
q.e: The path of revolution is the orbit.

q.t: Which star appears to stay still in the sky?
q.e: The Earth's axis points very close to the Pole Star, so it barely seems to move.

q.t: In a solar eclipse, which body blocks the Sun?
q.e: Sun → Moon → Earth: the Moon's shadow falls on the Earth.

q.t: In a lunar eclipse, which body's shadow falls on the Moon?
q.e: Sun → Earth → Moon: the Earth's shadow falls on the Moon.

q.t: Is it safe to look at a solar eclipse with the naked eye?
o: No — it can damage the eyes
q.e: The Sun is still intense enough to cause blindness. Use proper eclipse goggles or projection.

q.t: Is a lunar eclipse safe to watch with the naked eye?
q.e: You're looking at the dim Moon, not the Sun, so it's safe.

q.t: The Earth rotates from…
q.e: Because the Earth turns West→East, the Sun appears to rise in the East.

q.t: Why does the Sun appear to rise in the East?
o: The Earth rotates West to East
The Sun moves East to West around us
q.e: Like trees seeming to move past a merry-go-round, the Sun seems to move because we turn.

q.t: The main cause of seasons is…
o: The tilt of the Earth's axis
The Earth's distance from the Sun
q.e: The tilt changes how concentrated sunlight is and how long the day is.

q.t: What is the longest day in the Northern Hemisphere?
q.e: 21 June, the summer solstice.

q.t: On an equinox, day and night are each about…
q.e: Equal day and night — 'equinox' means equal night.

q.t: When India has winter, Australia has…
q.e: The Southern Hemisphere always has the opposite season.

q.t: During a total lunar eclipse, the Moon looks…
q.e: The fully shadowed Moon takes on a dark red colour.

q.t: Why do we see different stars in different months?
o: The Earth's night side faces a different direction as it revolves
q.e: As the Earth goes round the Sun, the night sky points to a different part of space.

q.t: Who explained the Earth's rotation using a boat example in the Aryabhatiya?
q.e: Just as a man in a moving boat sees the shore move back, we see stationary stars moving west.

q.t: Which pendulum demonstrated the Earth's rotation?
q.e: Léon Foucault's long pendulum gave the first simple demonstration; one hangs in India's new Parliament.

q.t: In June, why is the Northern Hemisphere hotter?
o: It is tilted towards the Sun — concentrated rays and longer days
It is closer to the Sun
q.e: Tilt towards the Sun means sunlight hits more directly (less spread out) and for more than 12 hours.

q.t: When is the Earth closest to the Sun?
q.e: In January — during northern winter. This proves distance isn't what causes seasons.

q.t: Why are seasons not very marked in south India?
o: It is near the equator, where day length stays about 12 h
It is closer to the Sun
q.e: Near the equator, day length and sun intensity change little through the year.

q.t: How can the small Moon cover the huge Sun?
o: The Moon is much closer, so their apparent sizes are similar
q.e: Apparent size depends on real size and distance — like your thumb covering a far-away head.

q.t: Why is a total solar eclipse seen from only a small area?
o: The Moon's shadow on Earth is small
q.e: The Moon's shadow covers only a narrow strip of Earth.

q.t: Why can many more people see a lunar eclipse?
o: Everyone on the night side can see the Moon
q.e: The Earth's big shadow covers the whole Moon, visible to the entire night side.

q.t: At the North Pole, the Sun rises around 21 March and sets around…
q.e: Six months of continuous daylight, then six months of darkness.

q.t: Venus is much bigger than the Moon. During a transit of Venus it looks like…
o: A small black dot on the Sun
q.e: Venus is so far away its apparent size is tiny.

q.t: A safe way to view a solar eclipse:
o: Project the Sun's image on a wall with a mirror
q.e: Projection, certified eclipse goggles, or a planetarium event are safe.

q.t: Why does a solar eclipse last only a few minutes at one place?
o: The shadow sweeps across due to Earth's rotation and Moon's motion
q.e: The Moon's shadow keeps moving across the Earth's surface.

q.t: A friend says 'summer happens because the tilted hemisphere is closer to the Sun'. Why is this wrong?
o: The distance difference is far too small to matter
The tilted part is farther away
q.e: Tilt changes the angle and day length of sunlight, not the distance in any meaningful way.

q.t: Arrange for a solar eclipse:
q.e: The Moon must sit between the Sun and the Earth.

q.t: A lunar eclipse can only happen at…
q.e: The Earth must be between the Sun and Moon, which is when the Moon's lit side faces us — full moon.

q.t: Why does the Pole Star seem not to move?
o: The Earth's axis points almost at it
q.e: Stars near the axis direction barely move as the Earth spins; the rest circle around it.

q.t: Aryabhata's value for one rotation was about…
q.e: About 23 h 56 min 4.1 s — very close to today's value.

q.t: On 22 December in the Northern Hemisphere:
q.e: It's the winter solstice.

q.t: A cricket team tours Australia in December. Which clothes to pack?
q.e: In December the Southern Hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun — summer.

q.t: Which observatory has recorded data about the Sun since 1899?
q.e: Kodaikanal Solar Observatory in the Palani hills, run by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics.

q.t: Who is called the father of modern Indian astronomy?
q.e: Vainu Bappu set up telescopes at Kavalur and Nainital and discovered a comet.

q.t: Which combination causes seasons?
o: Tilted axis plus the Earth revolving around the Sun
q.e: The tilt stays fixed in space; as the Earth revolves, first one hemisphere then the other leans towards the Sun.
